content: Authoritative multiplayer server patterns keep one canonical state machine per room on the server (event-driven statechart such as XState, or a hand-rolled switch-based FSM), driving phase transitions from server-side timers (setTimeout/interval) rather than client clocks; clients only send intents (submit caption, submit vote) and receive broadcast state snapshots. Frameworks like Colyseus formalize this authoritative-server model (server decides state, clients send inputs only) but for a small single-room one-week project a hand-rolled FSM on top of a plain WebSocket/Socket.IO server is lower-risk than adopting a new framework.
